title: streaming-reconstruction-guard-and-toolcall-stable-handback
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Fix partial-JSON reconstruction when SSE fragments split inside escaped sequences
Introduce reconstruction guard that prevents tool/function-call reorderings during stream replay
Improve OpenAI-compat layer to surface handback-fidelity metadata for client heuristics
description: Motivation: We observed a class of in-production incidents where SSE fragment splits inside escaped JSON strings or multi-byte UTF-8 sequences could cause downstream consumers to see re-ordered function/tool call boundaries or emit malformed partial JSON. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime 'reconstruction guard' that assigns per-fragment fidelity credits and a deterministic handback protocol to ensure toolcall boundaries remain ordered across retransmit/replay and partial-frame repair. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/streaming: add FragmentFidelityLedger and a reconstruction guard that tracks credit windows and stalls handback until a safe boundary is observed or the ledger times out; 2) sse/parser: introduce escape-aware tail rewriter to avoid splitting inside escapes and normalize trailing delimiters before emission; 3) compat/openai: emit X-Redwood-Handback-Fidelity header and annotate stream events with handback_id so OpenAI-compat clients can prefer resumable handoff points; 4) protocol: deterministic toolcall handoff algorithm that converts ephemeral function-call tokens into ordered handback checkpoints to prevent interleaving when fragments arrive out-of-order; 5) tests: large suite of synthetic fragment replays and property tests that simulate jittered, coalesced, and reordered chunks. Implementation notes: The reconstruction guard uses a small in-memory ledger per connection (bounded to 32 entries) and a sliding credit window to avoid unbounded buffering. When ledger credit is insufficient, the connection flushes an escape-normalized delimiter and advances a handback checkpoint; this behavior preserves low-latency in common cases while preventing rare misorders. The OpenAI-compat annotations are backward compatible: older clients ignore handback_id and continue to operate normally. Checklist: - [x] Core runtime changes implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] End-to-end tests with python and ts SDKs - [x] Backwards compatibility validated against existing OpenAI-compat integration tests - [x] Performance microbenchmarks show <0.6% median latency regression on p4d for synthetic workloads - [x] Feature flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_reconstruct_guard rollout plan: feature off in production initial cut; enable for 10% traffic with canary instrumentation and latency/error dashboards; expand to 100% after 48h with no regressions. Related: ENG-2407 describes incident notes and replay corpus. This description includes small illustrative pseudo-patch: "if (fragment.endsWith('\\') || insideEscape(fragment)) normalizeEscapeTail(fragment)" which is implemented in sse/parser/tail_rewrite.go.

review_conversation: Mateo Ruiz: Please explain how the ledger bound interacts with long-running streams; are we at risk of dropping fidelity for very chatty sessions? Ava Chen: Ledger is per-connection and bounded to 32 entries by default; for chatty sessions we prefer more frequent handbacks so credit churn is lower rather than unbounded buffering. Janelle Park: Can you show the perf delta on p3/p4? Ava Chen: Microbenchmarks included, median latency regressions are <0.6% on p4d and tail changes are within noise. Samuel Becker: Add a unit test for splitting inside a 4-byte UTF8 codepoint. Ava Chen: Added property test that injects multibyte boundary splits and verifies JSON reassembly and call order. Mateo Ruiz: Approved. Janelle Park: Approved. Samuel Becker: Approved after requested test added.

notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind runtime.feature.streaming_reconstruct_guard. To roll back disable the flag in the feature service and restart stream-workers in a staged fashion. If misordering symptoms appear, enable compat/openai.vet_handback_checks and consult the fragment replay logs (tag: fragment-replay).
testing_summary: Unit tests: 98 new cases covering escape tails, multi-byte utf8 splits, and toolcall order; Integration: SDK e2e verifies end-to-end ordered function calls under chunk jitter; Perf: microbench suite on p4d and p3 shows negligible median impact and tail P95 within 2%
